extracted.intended_audience: Authors and implementers of MathML (MathML authors, renderer developers, converter/tool authors, accessibility tool authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authoring and rendering MathML presentation elements: how to mark up text, group sub-expressions, and use presentation elements and attributes so renderers and converters produce correct visual, aural, and semantic results.

rubrics_metrics.name: ms element (string literal) usage and rendering
rubrics_metrics.description: String-literal content should be encoded using the ms element; ordinary text inside math should use mtext (or sometimes mo or mi), but not ms. The strings encoded by ms are made up of characters / mglyphs rather than ASCII strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ms content should be rendered with visible escaping of certain characters (including at least the left and right quoting characters, and preferably whitespace other than individual space characters) so the viewer can see that the expression is a string literal and which characters form its content. Example: <ms>&</ms> represents a single & character; <ms>&amp;</ms> represents five characters starting with &. Note: ms elements trim and collapse whitespace according to 2.1.7, so whitespace intended to remain must be encoded as described there. ms accepts additional attributes lquote and rquote (defaults U+0022) to specify opening/closing quote characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mtext (not ms) for ordinary text embedded in math
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary (non-string-literal) text embedded in an expression should be marked up with mtext, or in some cases mo or mi, but never with ms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should choose mtext/mo/mi according to the nature of the text; ms is specifically for string literals (mglyph-based).

rubrics_metrics.name: mrow/a for horizontal grouping and directionality
rubrics_metrics.description: An mrow or a element groups sub-expressions (operators and operands) into a horizontal row; they are typically rendered left-to-right in LTR contexts or right-to-left in RTL contexts. The dir attribute may override inherited directionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several elements implicitly treat their arguments as if contained in an mrow (inferred mrow). Spacing between operators and operands is assumed to be added by mo elements (or embellished operators), not by mrows. Linebreaking (automatic/manual) always happens within mrows; control of linebreaking is via attributes on other elements. In MathML 4, mrow and a have identical behavior; use a for hyperlink compatibility when href is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group sub-expressions according to the expression's syntax tree
rubrics_metrics.description: Document authors should group sub-expressions using mrow in the same way they are grouped in the mathematical interpretation (i.e., follow the underlying syntax tree). Operators and their mathematical arguments should occur in a single mrow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper grouping improves spacing, allows better linebreaking and indentation, and simplifies semantic interpretation for CAS and audio renderers. More than one operator should occur directly in one mrow only when they can be considered to act together on interleaved arguments (e.g., parentheses and their content, chains of relational operators, or sequences separated by + and -). Renderers must not assume authors always follow these rules (any grouping is allowed syntactically).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence rule for mrow with one argument
rubrics_metrics.description: An mrow containing exactly one argument must be treated as equivalent to that single argument in all ways, provided the mrow has no attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the mrow has attributes, no equivalence requirement is imposed. This simplifies MathML-generating tools and affects definitions of embellished operators, space-like elements, and default form determination for mo elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise rule for grouping adjacent operators when generating MathML
rubrics_metrics.description: Two adjacent operators (possibly embellished and possibly separated by operands) should be in the same mrow only when the leading operator has an infix or prefix form (perhaps inferred), the following operator has an infix or postfix form, and the operators have the same priority in the operator dictionary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In all other cases, nested mrows should be used. When forming a nested mrow that includes just one of two successive operators of the mentioned forms, determine which operator acts on the intervening operands (preferably using original-expression precedence). This rule only affects recommended generation from other formats and does not change MathML validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: mfrac usage and numerator/denominator formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mfrac to mark fractions (and fraction-like objects such as binomial coefficients and Legendre symbols). Syntax: <mfrac> numerator denominator </mfrac>. mfrac sets displaystyle to false (or if already false increments scriptlevel by 1) within numerator and denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributes: linethickness (length | "thin" | "medium" | "thick", default medium; with OpenType Math fonts, medium should use MATH.MathConstants.fractionRuleThickness), numalign/denomalign ("left"|"center"|"right", default center), bevelled (boolean, default false) to request bevelled style (numerator/denominator separated by slash). A linethickness of "0" renders without a bar (useful for binomial coefficients). Thicker lines may be used with nested fractions. In RTL contexts the numerator leads (right) and diagonal slash slants accordingly; if a forward slash is desired in RTL, use alternative markup (e.g., an mo in an mrow). Note: MathML Core only allows <length-percentage> values for linethickness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color and drawing guidance for fraction line, surd and overbar
rubrics_metrics.description: The fraction line (if any), the surd and the overbar should be drawn using the color specified by the mathcolor attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may set mathcolor on corresponding elements; renderers should use mathcolor to color those visual rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: msqrt and mroot semantics and scriptlevel/displaystyle behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Use msqrt for square roots and mroot for radicals with indices. Syntax: <msqrt>base</msqrt>, <mroot>base index</mroot>. mroot requires exactly two arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mroot increments scriptlevel by 2 and sets displaystyle to false within the index; msqrt leaves displaystyle and scriptlevel unchanged within its argument. In RTL contexts the surd begins on the right. msqrt/mroot accept attributes common to presentation elements; draw surd and overbar using mathcolor.

rubrics_metrics.name: mstyle to change style defaults for contained elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mstyle to make style changes that affect rendering of its contents by changing default attribute values for descendants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mstyle accepts attributes described in 3.1.9 and most attributes accepted by other presentation elements except certain disallowed ones. Effects differ by attribute type: inherited attributes (e.g., displaystyle, scriptlevel) set values that children inherit unless they override them; non-inherited attributes (e.g., linethickness on mfrac) set a new default for contained elements (overridden elements do not affect descendant default); computed attributes (e.g., stretchy, form) are overridden by mstyle. Note that MathML-Core may not support setting some of these attributes. mstyle directly accepts mathcolor and mathbackground; mathbackground fills the mstyle bounding box but does not set a default background color.

rubrics_metrics.name: mstyle attribute-name exceptions and scoping rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When mstyle shares attribute names with other elements, the attribute applies only to particular element types when set on mstyle (e.g., height/depth/width apply only to mspace; rowalign/columnalign apply only to mtable; lspace applies only to mo; align applies only to munder/mover/munderover).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain attributes such as src (which have no default values) cannot be set on mstyle. The voffset attribute of mpadded cannot be set on mstyle. Authors must be aware that setting attributes on mstyle may not have the same effect as setting them on the underlying element types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mstyle to prevent nested-fraction shrinking (practical example)
rubrics_metrics.description: In continued or nested fractions, use mstyle to reset displaystyle and scriptlevel for children of each mfrac so nested fractions don't shrink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example pattern: wrap numerators/denominators or inner fractions in <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> ... </mstyle> to keep sizes consistent across nested fractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: merror for inline error reporting in generated MathML
rubrics_metrics.description: Use merror to render an error message at the position where erroneous input occurred; its content can be any MathML expression or sequence and is intended to help indicate syntax errors detected by preprocessors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprocessors should replace erroneous input with an merror containing a clear, human-readable description of the error and (optionally) correctly formatted subsections of the original input. No specific message format is mandated; design messages to make clear what is wrong and how to fix it. merror accepts common presentation attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: mpadded for adjusting bounding box and positioning (no rescaling)
rubrics_metrics.description: mpadded renders its child's content unchanged but modifies the child's bounding box and the child positioning point according to mpadded's attributes; it does not rescale (stretch/shrink) content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common use is padding; mpadded can also shrink bounding box or move content and combinations (including negative padding) can cause overlap with neighboring content—use with care. Audio renderers are suggested to add/shorten time delays based on horizontal-space attributes (width, lspace). Renderers should ensure replacing mpadded by mrow with same content keeps relative spacing (except for attribute effects). MathML Core limits allowed attribute value types (length-percentage only); MathML4 extends syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: mpadded size and position attribute semantics (height/depth/width/lspace/voffset)
rubrics_metrics.description: mpadded attributes height, depth, width set or increment the bounding-box dimensions relative to the child content; lspace and voffset set the horizontal/vertical position of the child content relative to the mpadded positioning point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: height increases space above baseline (decreasing may cause overlap and should be avoided); depth increases space below baseline (decreasing may cause overlap); width controls horizontal distance between positioning point and following content (width=0 collapses spacing; decreasing may cause overprinting); lspace shifts the child horizontally (positive increases leading space, negative may cause overprinting; lspace does not affect width); voffset shifts vertically (positive raises rendering; negative lowers; does not affect height/depth). Absolute mpadded attribute values may not be portable across implementations because MathML does not define precise 'ink' vs bounding-box relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: mphantom for invisible alignment with preserved metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: mphantom renders invisibly but occupies the same size, depth, height and baseline position as its content; used to align parts of an expression by duplicating sub-expressions invisibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mphantom accepts a single argument and can be combined with mpadded. Renderers should ensure spacing with surrounding elements is the same as replacing mphantom with an mrow of the same content, even when linebreaking occurs. mphantom is not considered space-like unless its content is space-like. Be cautious: wrapping an mphantom around a subsequence of arguments can change default determination of the form attribute for mo elements inside it; to avoid spacing differences you may need to set form explicitly or wrap each argument in its own mphantom.

rubrics_metrics.name: mfenced convenience form and equivalence to expanded mrow form
rubrics_metrics.description: mfenced provides a convenient syntax for enclosed (fenced) expressions with optional separators; mfenced is equivalent to an expanded form using mrow and mo elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mfenced can contain zero or more arguments; if more than one argument, it inserts separators and uses a nested mrow for grouping. Renderers supporting the recommendation must render mfenced and its expanded form identically. Note: MathML-Core supports only the expanded form (authors/tools targeting MathML-Core should emit expanded mrow forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML-Core compatibility notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Some convenient or extended presentation features are not supported by MathML-Core or have restricted attribute value types in MathML-Core (e.g., mfenced convenience form; non-<length-percentage> linethickness/mpadded attributes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and converters should be aware of MathML-Core restrictions: emit expanded mrow forms (instead of mfenced) when targeting MathML-Core; use length-percentage values where required, and avoid relying on MathML3 pseudo-units or MathML4 namedspace when targeting MathML-Core.
